Question: Chrome/Edge started by the parity tool showed no page tree (0 lines); how to get a real read?
Choice: Launch Chrome/Edge with --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows and Firefox with widget.windows.window_occlusion_tracking.enabled=false (throwaway profiles only)
Why: Measured: a window opened behind others is occluded; Chromium builds no accessibility tree (even with --force-renderer-accessibility) and Firefox marks the front page offscreen. A user reads a page in front, so this reproduces the real condition.

Question: Where do fixture docs and the background-tab filter come from, and what about W1-6's ineffective node filter?
Choice: Fixtures from key_probe.read_keys (control+raw) + key_probe._typed; read_keys filters Documents by the CACHED IsOffscreen. core/ untouched (rule 6): the read_page_nodes filter bug goes to W2-5
Why: key_probe's node fields are the fixture format; onscreen_only's CurrentIsOffscreen raises on AutomationElementMode_None elements so every Document is kept. W1-7 is not allowed to change SGT capture.

Question: Service settings, on save: Sera shows 'will watch gst-like.gov.in for <service>' (D21). If the user answers No, what happens? A = nothing is saved, the edit dialog stays open so the link can be changed. B = the service is saved but its domain is not watched (Sera remembers this choice per service in a synced setting).
Choice: A
Why: asked as Q1

Question: Which services overlap rules apply when registering portals?
Choice: A domain equal to or covering/under Income Tax or GST is not registered (built-in wins); a domain overlapping one an earlier service (sort order) claimed is skipped; extra_domains only for portal names that are services; a single-label host gives no domain
Why: no duplicate portals for one domain; narrowest scope; built-ins stay untouched

Question: Part N: what counts as a value vote for a link position?
Choice: each distinct client once (VALUE_CLIENTS = 3, page votes 0), not each link pair
Why: R8: link-pair counting let 2 clients with 3 sibling pages mask a position, while many clients sharing 2 years never did; 3 keeps W1-4's tested 2-clients-not-enough / 3-clients-masked behaviour

Question: Part D: rarity weight of a value both compared captures show
Choice: count the compared pair as one capture: 1 / (rarity - 1)
Why: an equal value is always shown by both, an unequal one by one; literal 1/rarity halved agreement, so one changed value among 10 rare ones gave 0.82 (undecided) instead of 0.9 (same); blueprint says an ARN weighs 1

Question: Part D check: the two fictional local-page sessions should be one client
Choice: keep them undecided (no vote)
Why: counts on today's captures: per page 3 codes, 2 periods and 1 alphanumeric value differ (sim 0.70, was 0.56): not one client; the blueprint's expectation was wrong, undecided is the honest result (rule 6)

Question: How does memory match rejected signatures?
Choice: (link, shape, text) matching either self.link or self.page
Why: Allows callers to pass either resolved base link or page string cleanly

Question: Edge window title with profile name: strip only the zero-width space, or also the profile segment?
Choice: Allow zero-width spaces inside 'Microsoft Edge' in BROWSER_SUFFIX_RE only
Why: Chrome/Edge titles must not change; the leftover '- Profile 1' is stable and only used when the address bar is unreadable

Question: How to key Firefox-only line rules (dropdown options, doubled label)?
Choice: On the Document's framework id 'Gecko' (live CurrentFrameworkId / cached 30024); node trees carry gecko:true on the document's first node
Why: Blueprint rule: browser-dependent rules key on framework id; Chrome/Edge lines and nodes stay byte-identical

Question: Retirement follows time order, so forward/reversed builds can legitimately differ once 4+ clients exist; how is 'orders agree' kept meaningful?
Choice: The order check builds both orders with retire=False (PageMemory/build retire flag); the runner prints 'retired (time order): k' from the forward build
Why: Part H counts misses in a row by time; the order check is meant to prove alignment and verdicts do not depend on client order

Question: Part C rule 2 'changes with time': does a day seen by only one client count as agreement?
Choice: No: the texts must differ between days that 2+ clients were seen on
Why: Rule 6: two clients captured on different days with their own data would otherwise be called noise and their datapoint lost

Question: Which verdicts may a label candidate come from, given probably furniture asks for labels while verdicts are being computed?
Choice: Base verdict 'same for all clients' with a fixable or alphanumeric type, plus unpaired repeats of such a (shape, text)
Why: Same set as compare.py's fixed + variable_alignment + semi-variable alphanumeric (variable_alignment only ever comes from a fixable text); avoids the label -> verdict -> furniture -> label loop

Question: A node in a real table whose column has no name (or a header cell): what label?
Choice: Fall back to the screen-box rules (labels._label, which still tries the structural _table_label first)
Why: Blueprint: box rules apply to values outside any table and to tables without table markup; a nameless column gives the table nothing to say

Question: How do container moves reach suggest()?
Choice: moves={key: class} argument; override with reason 'moved by the user'
Why: sdis_decisions table does not exist before W4-4; the dict is what that reader will pass

Question: Which UIA worker does SDIS's raw read use?
Choice: Its own: the recorder thread joins the MTA and creates its own CUIAutomation8 (as sgt_i/uia_events); new uia_nodes.read_page_nodes_here reads on that thread; read_page_nodes unchanged
Why: read_page_nodes runs on vsdc_uia_text's single shared worker; a raw read still in flight when SGT's next read starts would make SGT abandon that worker and count toward UIA switching off (5 per run), which would change SGT capture (rule 6)

Question: How is a recorder session named for the engine?
Choice: record carries started (time of the session's first record this run); sources names it 'sgt <session id> <started>'
Why: identity._by_time orders sessions by their last word as a time; a bare SGT session id is random hex, so client order and retirement (time order) would be random

Question: Push trigger, batch size and repeat files
Choice: Any successful sync session triggers a push at most every 15 min on its own thread; a push carries at most 200 files / 200 MB (rest next time); a file written in the last 60 s is not finished; a re-pushed name replaces the stored copy (atomic .part + os.replace); names other than sdis_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl refuse the whole manifest
Why: Fits the transport's 600 s session deadline, never sends a file still being written, and a lost ack only causes a harmless resend

Question: Which captures folders does one mining run take, given pushed files sit in corpus/<device id>/ with the same day names on every PC?
Choice: One --captures folder per run, as mine() takes today; walking corpus/<device>/ plus sdis_capture (file keys by relative path) is left to the WP wiring the button (W4-5)
Why: mine() keys files by bare name, so a multi-folder run needs an engine change to state keys; out of W4-3's scope and not on the regression path

Question: Does the PyInstaller spec need core.sdis.mine_process added by hand?
Choice: No: build_tools has no .spec in the repo and no hand-listed hiddenimports; main.py imports the module statically so PyInstaller finds it
Why: grep of build_tools for hiddenimports found none; nothing to edit, no installer built

Question: Where the user's label lives in sdis_fields.json and how a registered spec is named
Choice: label in the spec's note (never its labels); spec name sdis.<field>; field slug never equal to an existing field (_2, _3 ...)
Why: the page labels decide capture, so a rename must not touch them; a bare field name would override a built-in spec of the same name in load_registry

Question: Which database file holds sdis_fields / sdis_decisions, and what an empty table writes
Choice: rawPayload.db next to tracker_dump (LWW on gid, retire = status update); no active rows -> sdis_fields.json removed; period/label/sentence/control datapoints are not registrable
Why: follows tracker_dump as the WP says; a missing file is exactly the pre-Part-Q spec set; no drafted pattern exists for those types, so no guessed spec

Question: Which containers count for the S.3 check 'a field is in at most one container per portal'?
Choice: Profile builder, Others and every dataset container of that portal
Why: Part S: every registered datapoint lives in exactly one container; the three kinds are all containers

Question: Loading sdis_containers.json on a PC has no database: check field names against sdis_mcl and portals against registered ones there?
Choice: No: put() and import run those two membership checks; load runs every other S.3 check
Why: the written file was checked when it was put; portal_names() at load would recurse through vsdc_scope -> config

Question: remove_field: what happens to a container's examples that captured the removed field, and class_exceptions vs a user's move?
Choice: examples capturing the removed field are dropped (the rest must still give their levels); a user's move beats class_exceptions, which beat the S.1 suggestion
Why: an example of a field combination that no longer exists cannot be checked; a move is the user's latest explicit choice

Question: sdis_config row identity and spec names for one field on several pages
Choice: the containers row has a fixed gid (md5 of 'sdis_config:containers'); specs are sdis.<field>, sdis.<field>.2, .3...; the same page (portal + page labels) re-uses its spec
Why: two PCs creating the row at once write the same LWW row, not two; spec names stay unique while SGT merges captures by field

Question: Register for a Dataset or Others datapoint
Choice: Add to sdis_mcl and the containers file only; no spec until SGT reads containers (W4-7)
Why: A dataset or Others field must not latch as a profile spec; register_field refuses them by design

Question: Mining reads one folder keyed by bare file name, but every PC has same-named day files
Choice: Find datapoints hard-links each device's sdis_*.jsonl into mine_input/ as sdis_<tag>__<name>
Why: Same-named files from different PCs would collide in mine(); names stay stable between runs so mining stays incremental

Question: A dataset container's tracker row is keyed by the canonical key (portal, client, form = container name, period). A container named after a built-in form (e.g. 'GSTR-3B submission') gets the SAME key as SGT's built-in GSTR-3B row. A: share that row (the tracker keeps one row per key and never lowers its status; the latest writer's details show). B: keep container rows apart by keying the form as the container name squeezed to letters+digits (e.g. GSTR3BSUBMISSION), so they never merge with built-in rows.
Choice: A
Why: asked as Q2

Question: How do SGT capture dataset and Others fields, and keep them out of its built-in dataset?
Choice: They register as current_dataset specs named sdis.<field>; SGT splits res.current by that name prefix and feeds those hits only to core/sgt/sgt_containers.py. A period-typed datapoint drafts the shape pattern of its values (miner type code).
Why: Profile specs latch, so dataset values must not be profile specs; the name prefix is the one global, already-reserved mark; a container needs its period field capturable.

Question: Carrier rows and the SRPF fold: key, status, when written, history
Choice: Carrier key = compute_dataset_key(portal, client, 'SDIS info', '') with status Not Submitted, written at session end only when no dispatched row carried the latest values (else the last sent row is re-queued). raw_aggregates history keeps changes only (an unchanged value carried again is no change); portal_profiles latch, a longer value containing the held one replaces it. core/sgt_i/sera_data.py is not filtered: carriers have no form or period, so SGT-I never matches them.
Why: One row per (client, portal), stable across sessions; the fold gives the same columns on re_resolve; keeps core/sgt_i untouched.

Question: core/sdis command lines (tables.py, link_map.py) printed page texts to the console
Choice: console gets counts only; tables.py --text writes the grids to output/tables_<file>.txt, link_map's texts stay in its CSV
Why: section 9.3: logs and console print counts, never values; the local output folder already holds the CSVs
